provenance: Codon usage is the RELATIVE FREQUENCY OF EACH CODON WITHIN ITS SYNONYMOUS FAMILY, so every family sums to 1. Only within-family ratios matter, which means a table pasted in per-1000 units works without conversion. E. coli, B. subtilis and S. cerevisiae are from the Kazusa Codon Usage Database via the python_codon_tables retriever; their genetic-code assignment was checked codon by codon. Halomonas has no genome-derived table here and carries an explicit mutational-equilibrium null model instead. V. natriegens has no table at all: usage is null, as parts.json does for an unresolved sequence.

organisms.name: Escherichia coli
organisms.blurb: The default bacterial expression host. Moderate GC, strong translational selection, extremely well characterised.

table.source: Kazusa CUD, taxid 316407 (E. coli K-12 W3110)
table.note: Retrieved with the python_codon_tables Kazusa retriever; genetic code checked codon by codon.

highSource.label: Sharp & Li 1987 highly-expressed E. coli index
highSource.note: Relative adaptiveness measured on highly expressed E. coli genes. This is the reference set CAI was originally defined against, and it differs sharply from the genome average: it prefers GCT for Ala, GGT for Gly and CGT for Arg, where the genome average prefers the GC-rich GCG, GGC and CGC. Sharpening the genome average would have pushed the wrong way, which is why a measured table matters here.

organisms.name: Saccharomyces cerevisiae
organisms.blurb: Budding yeast, and a eukaryote rather than a bacterium. AT-rich genome, strong bias in highly expressed genes, Crabtree-positive.

organisms.oxygenNote: Facultative; ferments well anaerobically given sterols and unsaturated fatty acids.

organisms.name: Halomonas elongata
organisms.blurb: High-GC halophilic Gammaproteobacterium. Grows from seawater-strength to hypersaline media; accumulates ectoine.

table.source: Mutational-equilibrium null model at genome GC 63.6 per cent
table.note: NOT a genome codon count. It encodes base composition only and carries no translational selection, so CAI against it means very little. Build a real table from CDS before reporting anything for this organism.

organisms.oxygenNote: Aerobic, with only limited anaerobic growth.

organisms.name: Vibrio natriegens
organisms.blurb: Fast-growing marine Gammaproteobacterium; doubling time under 15 min in salt-supplemented rich media. A plasmid host in this project, but no codon table is bundled.

table.note: No genome-derived V. natriegens codon table is bundled, and inventing one would be worse than admitting the gap. Paste V. natriegens CDS in the Codon table panel to count a real one, or optimize against E. coli, which is the closest bundled relative (both Gammaproteobacteria) and the conventional stand-in. Genome GC is recorded for reference only and is not used as a codon table.
